content: Can anyone at Axiomatic AI give some context behind the website: https://physlib.org/ (registered 10 days ago). This is not associated with this project, but uses both the names "Physlean" and "Physlib" in it.
This topic was moved here from #PhysLib > Website: https://physlib.org/ by Joseph Tooby-Smith.

@Leopoldo Sarra @Winston Yin (尹維晨) @Matteo Cipollina Is this trying to compete with this project? If not, why choose the same name, and a very similar url? I understand this may not directly be under the prevue of Axiomatic AI, but its seems related to Dirk Englund who is one of your founders.

Hi Joseph, thank you for pointing out. I was not aware of this website, as it seems to be related to an initiative of prof. Englund at MIT, unrelated to Axiomatic AI. I will get back to you as I get more details.
This topic was moved here from #PhysLib > Website by axiomatic ai? by Joseph Tooby-Smith.
Thanks for explaining @Leopoldo Sarra. Any update would be great. Have removed association with Axiomatic from title of this thread.

Oh no! It's like the CSlib naming collision...
Between this and https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26094 it seems like it'll get confusing fast...

My real issue with this one is both the use of "Physlean" and "Physlib". I do not believe this can be coincidental or accidental (although it maybe carelessness), given that I know Dirk Englund is aware of this project.
Presumably you have both names claimed on reservoir already?
@Eric Wieser We still appear as PhysLean on the reservoir I think.

The other side of this, is that I'm no longer sure where Axiomatic AI's commitments lie. Previously they have said they are keen to help the community here.

I know Leopoldo says this site is unrelated to Axiomatic AI, but Englund is their CSO and one of their founders. If he is planning on building a (to quote from that website)

...  machine-checkable library of physics, analogous to what Mathlib is for mathematics

I would assume that their priorities would turn to building that library up, not this one.

@Leopoldo Sarra if you could provide clarity on this point, it would be great. More generally the point of this project is that it is open-source and we can grow it together as a community, so if you know Dirk Englund has ideas of how we could make a project better for everyone, then it would be great if he was willing to share here.
Oh, I didn't catch that they have "PhysLean" in there too. Hm. Well, there's no code yet...

Joseph Tooby-Smith said:

undefined

Hi Joseph, Hi Folks -

I just learned of this!

FYI, I had actually started using "physlib" as far back as 2024 already in my group. We didn't have much online, but I shared some gh records with Joseph that show this just now in an email.

In any case, we didn't know that physlean had changed to physlib until last week!

Now that i've had a chance to catch up on the very substantial work done by this community, I am fine to transfer the domain or redirect or so. I've had it taken down in the meantime and am in touch with Joseph to finish.

Best regards, Dirk

Leopoldo Sarra said:

undefined

Btw as Leopoldo and Winston know, we have an 'open forum' at 1400 EST weekly at MIT and over zoom on topics of lean and engineering and physics. Is there a periodic online meeting for physlib? Would be good to create some connections between the teams.

Hi @Dirk Englund ,

I appreciate that our use of Physlib is not novel. But what I will say is that the decision to rename the project Physlib was made public in advance of it happening (even more in advance to the maintainers), and anyone had the opportunity to object but nobody did.

There isn’t a team here in the usual sense, just lots of people from different backgrounds openly working together because (I assume) they believe that having a project like this is what is best for humanity - similar to Mathlib. Thus while we do have online drop-in sessions (called cafe’s) on a somewhat regular interval, they do not include the points of view of everyone in the community (if that makes sense). We are somewhat overdue having such a cafe, so would be happy to organize one at a time which would work for you. Though I would encourage members of your team to join this Zulip and the conversations here, even just for the Lean and Mathlib side of things, this is where many of the important conversations are happening in this area

More generally, I have two questions for you here:
  1. Would you be interested in helping grow this project, and inputting what you have learned about formalization so we can improve things for everyone collectively? 

  1. If not, what are the barriers that are stopping you? Are they things that we can work to overcome?

Hi @Joseph Tooby-Smith , re Physlib : yes, all good! I just hadn't been following.

I agree fully with the mission and we will contribute !

  1. I'll have a meeting with team when i get back form Taiwan next week.
  2. None! We'll have a few topics to contribute to early May.

i'll call u regarding cafe or forum

ttys !
Nice sounds good @Dirk Englund . Have a good time in Taiwan!
